Appendix: Statistical Assumptions Checks

Methodological Note on Low Sample Size Limitation: Given the small run-level sample sizes (n=4–5 per condition), formal normality tests (Shapiro–Wilk) and homogeneity of variance tests (Levene) have limited statistical power and were used only as a supplementary check rather than a definitive decision criterion. Welch's t-test was preferred throughout for independent tests as it does not assume equal variances and is highly robust to minor departures from normality.
